forces.title: Transaction clearing commoditization shifts value from front-end interfaces.
forces.description: As transaction clearing becomes increasingly commoditized, value is relocating from visible front-end checkout screens to the invisible "control layer" of back-end trust, machine identity, consent engines, and dynamic routing protocols. This commoditization directly pressures the revenue and profitability of clearing houses, which are core market infrastructure entities.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Payments value shifts to invisible control layer infrastructure.
forces.description: The payments industry is experiencing a structural shift where value moves from visible customer interfaces (e.g., card swipes) to underlying infrastructure components like credentials, consent, identity, protocols, dynamic routing, risk, and policy control. This transformation means that ownership and development of this "infrastructure of trust" will become critical for capturing value in the evolving commerce landscape, impacting market infrastructure entities.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Global payment infrastructure fragments into regional, multi-rail competitive arenas.
forces.description: Contrary to predictions of global unification, the operational reality for financial services providers in Europe and globally is increasing fragmentation of payment infrastructure. This involves competing pressures from zero-fee domestic real-time A2A networks, legacy card perimeters, and wholesale stablecoin corridors, creating a complex multi-rail environment that market infrastructure entities must navigate for competitive advantage.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Agentic AI-driven routing erodes traditional fee pools and net interest income.
forces.description: Autonomous software agents are projected to dynamically route transactions and optimize financial decisions for consumers and corporations, minimizing fees and maximizing rewards. This capability poses a significant headwind to traditional payments revenue, including fee pools and net interest income for entities involved in clearing and settlement, potentially putting $75 billion globally at risk by 2030.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Stablecoins and tokenized assets bypass traditional FX and interchange.
forces.description: The scaling of digital assets like stablecoins and tokenized deposits presents a risk to traditional payments and deposit revenues. These instruments can bypass conventional interchange and foreign-exchange (FX) conversion markups, and shift float income from commercial bank deposits. This leads to direct margin pressure on FX spreads and correspondent banking fees, affecting exchanges and clearing houses involved in these services.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Geopolitical and regulatory fragmentation hinders cross-border payment infrastructure.
forces.description: National supervisory frameworks are viewed as primary pacing variables for payment rail innovation, with major markets pursuing monetary sovereignty rather than global standards. A European banking infrastructure executive highlights "supervisory divergence" as a question of sovereign liability for autonomous, cross-border transactions, creating challenges for interoperability and legal responsibility for market infrastructure.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Consolidation driven by rising IT costs and moderating revenue growth.
forces.description: Structural consolidation is seen as inevitable due to a financial imbalance: IT expenditures are projected to grow at 9% annually through 2030, while global payments revenue growth moderates to 4%. This cost pressure means massive scale or direct rail control become primary defenses against margin compression, affecting the operational and strategic landscape for market infrastructure entities.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Western Europe's card-resilient markets sustain existing payment infrastructure.
forces.description: Markets in Western Europe are categorized as "card-resilient," characterized by mature credit and debit card infrastructure, high adoption rates, entrenched merchant acceptance, and established consumer protection. This enduring dominance of card rails implies continued stability and revenue streams for the existing clearing and settlement infrastructure associated with these networks in the EU region.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Nonbank Market Makers capture share in electronic, commoditized flow products.
forces.description: Nonbank Market Makers (NBMMs) are taking 9-14% wallet share in asset classes for electronic and commoditized flow products like cash equities and exchange-traded funds. NBMMs leverage technological sophistication, superior liquidity provision, and risk management to offer speed and low-cost execution, creating a significant competitive headwind for traditional exchanges and trading platforms that facilitate these products.
forces.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

forces.title: Building "trust layer" positions critical for agent-directed routing.
forces.description: With autonomous software agents increasingly routing transactions dynamically based on cost, speed, and trust, players that enable agent-directed routing across multi-rail environments gain a competitive edge. Major networks, technology firms, and payment service providers are currently drafting emerging agentic protocols, making it critical for market infrastructure entities to build positions in this "trust layer" to capture future value.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Value shifts from visible checkout to invisible trust infrastructure in payments.
viewpoints.description: McKinsey views payments revenue as relocating from front-end customer interfaces to the underlying infrastructure of trust, identity, protocols, and dynamic routing. As transaction clearing becomes commoditized and agentic payments rise, the key strategic question shifts to ownership of this "control layer" infrastructure. Entities that build this layer first are poised to capture value, reshaping the economics beyond traditional transaction processing.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Payment infrastructure faces fragmentation, not global unification, requiring multi-rail navigation.
viewpoints.description: McKinsey believes that rather than converging to a single global standard, payment infrastructure is fragmenting into regional, multi-rail competitive environments. Financial services providers, including market infrastructure entities, must navigate this complexity, dealing with zero-fee domestic real-time networks, legacy card perimeters, and wholesale stablecoin corridors for cross-border settlement. This divergence poses strategic challenges for established infrastructure players.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Stablecoins and tokenized deposits are efficient wholesale settlement tools, not retail currencies.
viewpoints.description: McKinsey's interviewed executives largely perceive stablecoins and tokenized commercial bank deposits as highly efficient wholesale settlement tools, rather than consumer-facing retail currencies. Their primary advantage lies in illiquid or currency-constrained B2B corridors, where they can replace slow correspondent interbank settlement, operating alongside instant payment networks. This suggests a significant structural change in wholesale settlement for depositories and clearing houses.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

pnl_drivers.description: Lower interest rates compress treasury and deposit margins for financial institutions, including those operating market infrastructure services, prompting a shift towards fee-based revenue structures in the EMEA region.
A rapid shift to fee-based structures is observed as a response to margin compression, influencing how market infrastructure entities generate revenue.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of global payments revenue pools, segmented by geography and revenue type (net interest income vs. fee income). Specifically, EMEA's payments revenue growth is projected to slow to 3% annually in 2025–30, a sharp decline from 14% in 2020–25, driven by margin compression from lower interest rates and a shift to fee-based structures. This indirectly impacts market infrastructure entities' revenue growth in payments-related services.
market_sizing.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

pnl_drivers.description: Autonomous software agents dynamically route transactions and optimize financial decisions to minimize fees and maximize rewards, potentially eroding traditional fee pools and net interest income for market infrastructure entities.

AI-driven choices could lead to increased use of alternative or lower-cost payment rails, reducing revenue from traditional card networks and other established infrastructure for exchanges and clearing houses.

market_sizing.methodology: Forecasts for global payments revenue at risk due to agentic AI, with a baseline scenario of $75 billion by 2030. This includes potential declines in deposit net interest income ($65 billion) and consumer credit card revenues ($10 billion) from AI-driven optimization and payment rail substitution. This directly impacts revenue streams that exchanges and clearing houses might be exposed to (e.g., fee pools, FX routing).
market_sizing.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world
